subject: hydra
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: five-headed hydra.
Style: God of War.
reasoning:
I'm planning a dark, brutal God of War-style five-headed hydra design as a single TS module: a scarred, rune-carved reptilian body with five long necks each bearing a horned head with glowing eyes, plus a tail and four legs to work out.

Setting up joints and chains for the hips, spine, and tail with Catmull-Rom control points, then sweeping the body geometry with varying radii and belly shading sectors...

Now I'm laying out the five necks branching from the chest joint, computing offset positions for each neck's base, midpoints, and tip based on lateral spread.

Building the head shape as a frustum box from the head joint forward, using local direction words relative to the joint rather than world coordinates. I'm writing a small helper that resolves left/right based on sign so skull widening works symmetrically regardless of side.

Still shaping the skull...

eyes glowing ember spheres under dark brow ridges, with curved horns sweeping back via bezier arcs, small nostril spheres, outward cheek spikes, and a glowing rune scar placed on the body instead of the head.

Now I'm adding faint glowing rune outlines and warpaint cracks on the flanks, then setting up the four legs with hip/shoulder/foot positions and limb bend parameters for a believable stance.

Still writing leg and foot details...

For the armor, I'm thinking God of War style brutality — dorsal plates along the spine, iron bands or shackles around the hydra necks oriented to follow the neck curves, maybe with a glowing rune detail.

Now I'm adding battle scars too — slashing wounds embedded into the body's flank as thin glowing boxes, oriented against the surface normal to look like gouges.

I'm figuring out placement for three overlapping slashes at different azimuths and a slight spin for a natural slanted look, then moving on to belly plates and finalizing the color palette (scale tones, belly tan, bone white).

Now I'm deciding on texture: using a scales paint pattern for the body surface rather than flat color, applying it sparingly to the torso and neck to add visual interest while keeping other parts simple.

Working out proportions next: head roughly a meter long, neck around three meters, with the tail tip lowered near the ground and capped with a ring of bone spikes for a mace-like finish. Then I'm setting up the spine chain parented to the hips to drive the overall posture.

Setting up the hips root joint and running separate sweeps for the spine and tail chains so they share a matching radius where they meet, keeping the seam clean. I'm parenting the neck chain to the last spine joint, positioning its base inside the chest's radius near the top so it transitions smoothly into the body.

Now I'm plotting the five neck curves symmetrically around center, fanning them outward wider toward the tips so the heads spread apart at the ends while the bases stay tucked into the chest.

Setting up head and jaw joints at each neck's terminal point, oriented along the neck's forward direction, with the jaw as a small child joint offset below the head. I'm also defining the neck's tapering sweep radius and starting to lay out body sector boundaries like the belly region's angular range.

Now I'm sketching a helper for positioning points relative to the head using forward, up, and side vectors, then adding bony spikes along the neck sweep via the `along` traversal, oriented outward from the dorsal surface. I'm also considering adding small glowing rune marks somewhere on the body, though keeping that effect lightweight.

I'm planning rune-shaped marks on the shoulders made from thin boxes arranged like a rune glyph, placed using azimuth/elevation on the body surface with a guard for null hits, plus spiky bone pauldrons on the shoulders and a jagged ridge along the back to round out the armor details.

Now I'm adding a dark red mouth interior box between the jaws, and giving the jaw a slight open pose with a 12-degree rotation around the x-axis applied after all parts are built so the bones stay rigid.

Placing upper and lower teeth as small spike cones positioned along the jaw edges, tapering in size toward the back of the mouth, attached to the head and jaw bones respectively.

Adding nostril spheres near the snout tip, then planning horn shapes using a bezier sweep from base through a control point to the tip for a curved look.

For the center head I want a bigger crown, so I'm scaling up its horns and adding an extra midline crest of upward-back spikes. I'll give heads a size multiplier -- center largest, side heads slightly smaller -- and apply that scale factor to position offsets and radii.

One head gets a God of War style scar: left eye closed and slashed over with a dark bone-colored blinder instead of a glowing eye. Other eyes stay glowing spheres with a thin dark slit pupil box in front for detail.

Now I'm placing spine plates along the back using a spike generator that varies in length across several points along the body's sweep.

For iron bands, I'm adding thin torus rings around each neck at a point roughly 45% along its length, sizing the ring radius to match the neck's thickness there and orienting it using the chain point's tangent and nearest bone. I'll add a thinner rune-glow torus nearby as an accent.

For a few of the necks (say the first and fifth), I'm thinking of adding dangling chain links hanging down from the iron band, alternating their rotation for a loose chain-link look.

Then for the legs I'm adding claw details and knee spikes—small bone-colored spikes jutting backward/outward at each knee joint—before moving on to sweep the leg geometry along its chain with the right scale coloring.

Now I'm working out the limb function, which returns joint points from root to tip that feed into chain construction with proper parenting: hind legs parent to the hips, forelegs to the last spine joint, with bend angles configured so elbows angle back and knees angle forward.

I'm also sketching a body-radius profile using sine-based tapering to shape the spine sweep, with slightly flatter vertical radius than horizontal.

Mapping out the tail chain with five segments tapering from the hips down to a small spiky tip, adding spikes along the way and a club-like end bone. I'm also checking belly color placement, floor/feet alignment at y=0, and setting up the final module export to return the root bone.

Now I'm writing a slash-rune helper that generates energy slashes using thin boxes with a glow effect, positioning them near the shoulders at specific azimuth and elevation angles with spin rotation for a dynamic flow effect.

Writing head-building helper function...

Still shaping jaw geometry...

I'm setting up the mouth gap between upper and lower jaw, then defining shared scale paint textures for head and body in darker greenish tones. Next I need to tackle teeth, horns, and eyes.

Writing cheek spikes and chin barbels...

Now I'm plotting the horn curve as a bezier path running from near the brow up and back.

I'm finishing with pose placement, adding the jaw pose inside the head function after the builds, and trimming imports down to only what's actually used—THREE, createBuilder, catmull, bezier, limb, scales, and glow—skipping rng since it's unused.
